correctness.rationale: On the specified indexed four-agent profile every pair either contains the reporter (cost min(|r|,1)) or not (cost one); the resulting exact rational cost and strict improvement condition are derived with positive denominators. Convexity in the exponent and two positive polynomial certificates rule out all reports for 0<alpha<=2. The fixed deviation -1/5 has increasing advantage for all alpha>=3. At alpha=3 exact cubic factorization, strict concavity and negative positive-report branch give the entire manipulation interval. The exact script reproduces 805 cost evaluations and 322 local comparisons; enumeration alone is not used as proof.

value.rationale: A natural design change to a recently introduced strategyproof lottery is to strengthen preference for widely separated facility pairs using distance powers. The theorem proves that such a change creates incentives to misreport throughout an unbounded real-exponent family, while retaining exact local immunity over the interval up to two and completely classifying cubic profitable reports. This is structural mechanism-sensitivity evidence, not a numerical example or mere reformulation; it does not claim a fully classified global strategyproofness threshold.
